title: The Judgment of Solomon
text:
Two women came before King Solomon with a baby. They lived together in the same house, and each had given birth to a son, three days apart. There had been no one else in the house.

The first woman told the king what had happened. During the night, the other woman's baby had died, because she had lain on him in her sleep. She had then got up at midnight, taken the first woman's living son from beside her, and put her dead child in his place. In the morning, when the first woman went to nurse her baby, she found him dead, but looking closely, she saw it was not her son. The second woman insisted it was a lie: the living child was hers. They argued back and forth in front of the king.

Solomon called for a sword. When it was brought, he gave his order: cut the living child in two, and give half to one woman and half to the other.

At once the real mother, overwhelmed with love for her son, cried out to the king to give the baby to the other woman, and not to kill him. The other woman said: let him be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two.

The king then ruled: give the living baby to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is his mother. When all Israel heard the verdict, they held the king in awe.
lesson: When stories conflict and evidence is missing, design a choice that only the honest party would make. How people react under pressure reveals what they truly want.
date: ancient Israelite tradition, set c. 10th century BC
caveat: The story is part of the biblical account of Solomon and is not independently attested.
